articles.title: Turkiye highway crash kills 11, injures 27 after tour bus hits truck
articles.summary: Police detain tour bus driver after highway collision in western Turkiye leaves 11 dead and 27 injured.
articles.body:
At least 11 people have been killed and 27 injured after a tour bus and a tow truck collided in western Turkiye.

The crash happened near toll booths at Akhisar on the Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir highway in Manisa province on Sunday morning.

According to a statement from the Manisa governor’s office, authorities received a report of the collision just after 11am local time.

The wounded were taken to local hospitals , including the bus driver, who was detained by police following his discharge.

Images from the scene showed blue body bags lined along the roadside next to the overturned bus, which sustained heavy structural damage to its rear section.

The tow truck, which appeared to be carrying wooden planks, had also overturned.

Writing on social media platform X, Turkiye’s Interior Minister, Mustafa Ciftci, referred to the victims as citizens, though authorities have not yet confirmed whether any foreign nationals were among the casualties.

The governor of Manisa, Vahdettin Ozkan, visited the crash site as emergency teams cleared the wreckage.

“Work at the scene is currently ongoing under the coordination of the Public Prosecutor’s Office,” Ozkan said. “We are experiencing, in a painful way, just how vital it is to strictly adhere to traffic rules.”

articles.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Donald Tusk
articles.summary: Police received credible information about possible attacks against Donald Tusk and his defence minister.
articles.body:
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a man accused of plotting an assassination attack against him and his defence minister has been detained.

The interior ministry earlier reported that police had received credible information about possible attacks against Tusk and Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.

Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about the planned attacks, with a spokesman saying officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious".

Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in arresting the suspect.

The suspect was arrested in the Lower Silesia region and was a Polish national, Jacek Dobrzynski, a spokesman for the Special Services Co-ordinator told local media.

"In this case we are talking about a strong likelihood that these threats could actually be carried out," he said.

The plan was uncovered when an email with information about the potential attack was forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Galecka said.

Tusk has been Polish prime minister since 2023, having previously held the office from 2007 to 2014.

He served as president of the European Council from 2014 to 2019.

articles.title: Another showdown in Delhi? INDIA bloc to hold protest over CEC; CJP gives 24-hour ultimatum
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress and other opposition parties will march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12, demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress and other opposition parties will march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12, demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest comes a day after a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi and amid fresh political tensions over the alleged misuse of force against protesters.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has called on young people, opposition parties and civil society groups to join the march. The Congress has named it "Chalo Delhi - March for Democracy" and said participants will assemble at 1.30pm at the Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road junction.The opposition plans to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, demanding an end to alleged "vote chori", a halt to SIR and Kumar's resignation. However, sources said on Sunday night that the CJI had not agreed to meet Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, who had sought an appointment between 4pm and 5pm on Monday.Rahul, in a post on X, urged people to unite beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. "Yesterday, the nation's young came out in Delhi to peacefully protest. They came with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger. They were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons. This is not the India we want," he said."Tomorrow, we will march to the Supreme Court as Indians, united beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us," he added.Supreme Court steps in after crackdownThe march follows Saturday's police action against protesters demanding Kumar's removal. Several demonstrators, including activists of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), were detained as security personnel prevented them from reaching the designated protest site.On Sunday, the Supreme Court directed authorities to immediately lift prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita around the apex court complex. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said peaceful citizens should not face illegal detention and that movement across Delhi must be allowed in accordance with the law.The court was hearing petitions challenging the police crackdown and detentions, along with a contempt plea alleging disobedience of its orders.Meanwhile, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after he was allegedly manhandled by police during Sunday's protest. He later sought an independent investigation and accountability from the President, the Rajya Sabha chairman and the CJI.Brittas alleged that police personnel dragged him for around 50 metres, forcibly put him in a vehicle and assaulted him inside it before leaving him by the roadside. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor condemned the alleged mistreatment and called for an investigation.CJP vows to return to streetsCJP activists also vowed to continue their agitation after Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released following their preventive detention."We will take to the streets again; we will not be intimidated by people like Amit Shah and Modi. Throw us in jail not just once, but a hundred times," Dipke said.Delhi Police DCP Neha Yadav defended the detentions, citing alleged law-and-order violations during previous demonstrations, including stone-pelting, arson and damage to public property. She said prohibitory orders had been imposed in several areas to maintain public safety.Opposition leaders, however, accused the government of suppressing dissent. RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said "an Emergency has been declared", while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that women protesters had been mistreated.BJP hits back at oppositionThe BJP dismissed the allegations and accused the opposition of creating chaos. Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said the opposition "occasionally makes its presence felt, much like a cockroach crawling across one's back."BJP leader Karuna Sagar also challenged Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders to follow the constitutional procedure for removing the CEC. He said any evidence of wrongdoing should be presented before Parliament.Union minister of state Tokhan Sahu defended the electoral roll revision process, saying it had taken place under successive governments. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also criticised the opposition protests and praised Delhi Police for maintaining public safety.The latest confrontation follows the opposition's earlier march from Parliament to Vijay Chowk, after which INDIA bloc leaders submitted a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu. The Congress and its allies are now seeking to take their demands to the Supreme Court as the dispute over electoral rolls and Kumar's position intensifies.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: PM says it is 'clear' Russia interfered with Brexit referendum
articles.summary: He says voters were not "sufficiently" informed about how foreign actors sought to disrupt UK democracy.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said Russia did interfere with the Brexit referendum and warned that similar activities were taking place in France and Germany.

The prime minister told The Rest is Politics podcast that upon arriving in No 10, he had asked about possible Russian interference in the 2016 vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was."

"I think we've been too much on the back foot on that actually and we haven't informed people sufficiently about the extent to which people are seeking to disrupt the political process from overseas," he added.

Burnham did not provide further details about the type or extent of Moscow's activity during the Brexit referendum.

Britain Unbound, a pro-Brexit campaign group, said Burnham's comments were "another crude attempt to undermine the legitimacy of the decision that the British people made in 2016".

It said that foreign interference in UK elections was "obviously unacceptable" but added: "There is no good reason to believe that Russian intervention influenced the outcome of the referendum in 2016.

"It is also insulting to suggest that voters were so easily duped."

In his interview, due to be released on Monday, Burnham said he had discussed the problem of Russian interference with Chancellor Friedrich Merz during his visit to Germany earlier this week.

"There is certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics," he said.

He continued: "These things are important now to put clearly on the record and I believe help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies, namely Russia."

It is the first time a UK prime minister has said Russia sought to sway the 2016 Brexit poll but there have long been warnings about efforts by the Kremlin to exert influence on UK politics.

In 2020, Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee published a report into Russian interventions in UK elections and referendums.

It did not provide a definitive conclusion on whether Russia had attempted to influence the results of the EU referendum but did criticise successive governments for failing to fully assess or counter the threat.

In response, the Russian foreign minister dismissed the report out of hand and called it "Russophobia".

And a Kremlin spokesman said Russia did not meddle in other countries' elections.

In the same year, however, the then-Conservative government said it was "almost certain that Russian actors sought to interfere" in the 2019 general election.

BBC Verify has tracked Russian-linked disinformation campaigns including using AI to create fake videos which impersonate journalists and news organisations reporting on Ukraine.

One fake news website falsely claimed that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had bought a mansion owned by King Charles at a discounted price.

Earlier this year, Vijay Rangarajan, head of the UK Electoral Commission, told MPs that Russian deepfake videos had been "used extensively in elections around the world".

"There is no reason to assume Britain would be an exception," he added.

Last month, during his speech to the United Nations, Burnham accused Russian agencies of using "every means at their disposal to spread lies and disinformation and prey on people's fears".

He announced that the UK would set up a new centre to "stem the poisonous tide" of disinformation.

A Downing Street spokesperson said: "We are focused on ensuring our citizens and our institutions are protected from foreign powers and their proxies seeking to threaten lives and undermine our democratic values.

"We are doing this by strengthening our powers through the National Security Act, strengthening the resilience of our institutions and critical national infrastructure, strengthening our borders, and strengthening our police and intelligence agencies."

articles.title: Day or night, Chennai city swelters through endless power cuts
articles.summary: Chennai faces hours-long power cuts as TNPDCL cites cable faults, equipment failures and maintenance; outages hit suburbs and Tiruvallur amid protests.
articles.body: Chennai: Power cuts continued in the city and its suburbs, even on a Sunday, with several residential neighbourhoods reporting outages that lasted hours. Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL) continues to cite cable faults, equipment failures, and maintenance work as reasons for the disruptions.Power supply was affected in Ezhil Nagar and Tsunami Nagar in Okkiyam Thoraipakkam on Sunday afternoon after a fault developed in a 300 sqmm high-tension underground cable on the 11 kV Ezhil Nagar feeder. The power cut lasted for about three hours. In Velachery, the high-tension underground cable of the 11 kV Ram Nagar feeder was damaged during stormwater drain work in the morning. This led to a blackout in VOC Nagar.Similarly, residents of Aravamuthan Garden Street in Vepery reported a power disruption due to a fault in an underground cable. In Mylapore, there was no power from 10am to 4.30pm due to a fault in the 240 mm main underground power cable.“Though it is Oct, it feels like April, and the extreme heat causes heavy discomfort even for a minute without electricity,” said Vignesh Kumar, a resident of Kottivakkam.Meanwhile, maintenance work on the distribution box and transformer on the 11 kV ECR feeder under the Kottivakkam substation was carried out on Sunday, causing power cuts in surrounding areas. Similarly, maintenance work was cited as the cause of power cuts in Tiruvottiyur.A five-hour power cut in Tiruvallur district forced people to throng the Chennai-Kolkata National Highway to protest. They said they had been facing the same problem every other day, with no clarification from TNPDCL officials.When contacted, TNDPCL officials said the power outage in Tiruvallur was due to a fault in a busbar and insulator at the 110 kV section of the 230 kV Gummidipoondi substation. “The outage affected Gummidipoondi, SIPCOT (Phases 1, 2 and 4), Panchetti, Ponneri and Thandalam. articles.title: Vyapar Kendra, Galleria market roads in Gurgaon to revert to 2-way traffic after 11 years
articles.summary: GMDA to restore two-way traffic on Gurgaon’s Vyapar Kendra and Galleria Market roads after 11 years, aiming to cut diversions; residents warn of congestion risks.
articles.body: Gurgaon: After nearly 11 years of one-way traffic management, Vyapar Kendra Road and Galleria Market Road are set to revert to two-way traffic. GMDA has begun installing plastic divider bollards along Vyapar Kendra Road. The widening of both roads in New Gurgaon is almost complete, with finishing work underway.The proposed change is expected to reduce the need for motorists to take diversions and offer more direct connectivity. However, residents have raised concerns that restoring two-way traffic without adequate planning and enforcement could bring back congestion on roads that were converted to one-way stretches to ease traffic pressure.The roads serve Galleria Market, Sushant Arcade Market and Vyapar Kendra Road, besides catering to residents of Sushant Lok-I, spread across around 600 acres, and sectors 27, 28 and 43. Around 11 years ago, former deputy commissioner of police Bharti Arora introduced the one-way system on the two roads in view of increasing traffic and recurring jams. The arrangement improved traffic movement and provided relief to commuters. With the roads now widened, the authorities are preparing to restore movement in both directions.While two-way movement could improve connectivity for these neighbourhoods, roadside fruit vendors and other hawkers, along with encroachments, remain a concern. Residents fear that increased vehicle movement, coupled with roadside obstructions, could narrow the effective carriageway and create bottlenecks, particularly around busy market stretches. They said traffic management and control of encroachments would be crucial to ensuring that the change delivers the intended benefits.Municipal councillor from ward 22 Vikas Yadav said a traffic survey should be conducted before implementing the new arrangement to assess vehicle volumes and determine whether the widened roads can accommodate traffic in both directions. “People have been accustomed to the one-way system for 11 years. If roadside vendors and encroachments are not regulated, congestion could increase again,” he said.Yadav also raised concerns over the use of plastic divider bollards, saying they may not adequately prevent vehicles from entering the opposite lane if a driver loses control. Headlight glare from oncoming vehicles could also affect motorists at night. He called for a suitable divider and robust road safety measures before the change is implemented.General secretary of Sector 43 Residents Welfare Association Narendra Mehta suggested installing large concrete planters at short intervals along the centre of the roads. “Planting greenery in these planters would not only separate traffic moving in opposite directions but also improve the streetscape,” he said.Residents said the final traffic arrangement should take into account road capacity, market activity, pedestrian movement and accident risks. articles.title: War and high debt to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
articles.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran and its inflationary impact will dominate the agenda.
articles.body:
Finance officials from around the world will gather in Bangkok this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest-ever energy supply shock and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.

The US-Israel war on Iran, now in its eighth month, and its inflationary impact are slated to dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, held outside Washington for the first time in three years.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told Reuters News Agency that 18,000 people were registered to attend the meetings, 4,000 more than the last off-site meetings held in Morocco in October 2023.

Notably absent will be United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handles some “domestic engagements”, a US official said. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Kevin Warsh will attend and is slated to participate in a public event with Georgieva on October 16.

Several other finance ministers were also staying home due to domestic budget and election duties, but most central bankers would attend, Georgieva said.

Bessent’s decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 (G20) major economies, which the US leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine’s battle against Russia’s invasion, and the US move to impose sanctions on the International Criminal Court.

The Group of Seven (G7) countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower petrol prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of US sanctions designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its ‌‌war on Ukraine. The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

More than one billion barrels of oil have been released, mainly from onshore commercial inventories, since the start of the war on February 28. But industry executives say the amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fuelling pressure on prices.

The IMF has signalled little change in its forecast for three percent global growth in 2026, and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher. But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia’s invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.

IMF research released on Tuesday showed that sharp spikes in food and energy prices are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability.

One headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War II and will exceed 100 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) before 2030.

Advanced economies, led by the US, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, weather extremes triggered by the El Nino climate phenomenon, and a lack of investment in artificial intelligence (AI), which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries.

Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Together, they face $400bn in debt payments to external creditors in 2026, and interest payments already exceed 10 percent of revenue on average.

Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programmes that call for fewer but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures.
